children: MED-002 MED-003 MED-004 MED-005 MED-006 MED-008
rationale: Per-medicine detail questions only make sense when a medicine exists. Requires 'no regular medicines' AND every universal medicine screen (insulin, GLP-1, SGLT2, blood thinner, antiplatelet, steroid, opioid, sedative, patch, biologic, chemo, supplements, OTC) answered no. Last dose (MED-007) and recent change (MED-009) are deliberately kept.

children: ENDO-002 ENDO-003 ENDO-004 ENDO-005 ENDO-006 ENDO-007 ENDO-008 ENDO-009
rationale: Diabetes detail questions (type, insulin, pump, CGM, hypos, DKA, HbA1c) are triggered by 'known diabetes or diabetes treatment'. Requires no diabetes AND no insulin, GLP-1/GIP or SGLT2 medicine.
CKD stage is only asked with known CKD.
Dialysis modality, schedule, last session and access: trigger is 'dialysis or advanced CKD'. Requires no dialysis AND no CKD.

children: OSA-002 OSA-003 OSA-012 OSA-013 OSA-014 OSA-015 OSA-016
rationale: Sleep study, severity and PAP device questions are triggered by known OSA. Snoring/tiredness/witnessed-apnoea screening (OSA-004..006) is universal and stays.

children: ALL-002 ALL-003 ALL-004 ALL-005 ALL-006 ALL-007 ALL-008 ALL-009 ALL-010
rationale: Per-allergy details (agent, reaction, timing, severity, treatment, admission, re-exposure, testing, documentation). Requires no known allergy AND no previous perioperative reaction. An EMR-listed allergy that contradicts the patient's 'no' creates a conflict, which keeps these questions. Latex, chlorhexidine and uncertain-label screens (ALL-012/013/015) stay.

Previous general anaesthetic and sedation imply a previous operation/procedure. Previous spinal/epidural/nerve block (ANAES-003) is deliberately kept: a labour epidural may not be thought of as a 'procedure'.

children: ANAES-005 ANAES-006 ANAES-007 ANAES-008 ANAES-009 ANAES-010 ANAES-011 ANAES-012 ANAES-013 ANAES-014 ANAES-015 ANAES-016 ANAES-017 ANAES-018 PSY-009 RES-017
rationale: Prior anaesthetic complications, difficult airway/IV access, previous record, difficult post-op pain and post-op confusion all require prior anaesthesia or surgery. Requires no previous operation/procedure AND no previous regional anaesthetic. The universal perioperative-reaction screen (ALL-011) still covers anaphylaxis.

children: FAM-003 FAM-004 FAM-005 FAM-006 FAM-007 FAM-008
rationale: Family anaesthetic-history details. Requires no family anaesthetic problem AND no personal neuromuscular disorder. Malignant hyperthermia (FAM-002) is deliberately always asked because of its severity.

children: PSY-002 PSY-003 PSY-004 PSY-005 PSY-006 PSY-010 PSY-011
rationale: Chronic pain location, cause, severity, impact, pain specialist, implanted pump and spinal cord stimulator require chronic pain.
Opioid dose/frequency requires regular opioid use (both opioid screens answered no).
Cigarettes per day requires current smoking. Smoking duration and cessation date (PSY-020/021) stay so ex-smokers are still captured.
Drinks per day and binge frequency require current drinking. Past withdrawal/dependence (PSY-026) is kept: a current non-drinker may have a history.
Number of falls requires a fall in the last 12 months.
Amount of weight lost requires unintentional weight loss.
Duration of reduced intake requires reduced intake.
Transfusion reaction requires a previous transfusion.
Which blood products are acceptable only applies if some are declined.
Cirrhosis, varices, ascites and recent decompensation are triggered by known liver disease. Hepatitis (GI-014) is kept: past hepatitis may not be thought of as 'liver disease'.
Most recent seizure requires a history of seizures/epilepsy.
Reflux frequency/severity requires reflux. Regurgitation and aspiration history (GI-004/005) stay for aspiration safety.
Atrial fibrillation/flutter: requires no known abnormal rhythm AND no palpitations.
Coronary stent and bypass surgery: requires no coronary heart disease, no heart attack and no angina.
Lung-condition flare-ups and steroids for breathing require a known chronic lung disease (asthma, COPD, bronchiectasis, ILD or other).
Last menstrual period is relevant only if pregnancy is possible. The interviewer waits for the pregnancy question before asking this.
